landing.title: Hire on evidence, not impressions.

demo.label: A scene from an assessment
demo.message: Two of our three trucks are stuck at the port. The Henderson order is due at 4pm and they’ve already complained twice this month. What do you do first?
demo.answerStart: I’d call Henderson before ten and offer a split delivery:
demo.answerEvidence: half today from the Riyadh stock, the rest first thing tomorrow,
demo.answerEnd: then rebook the port slot. If they need it all today, I’ll know early enough to hire a third truck.
demo.note: The band narrows as evidence comes in, and the tick is the level the role needs. The highlighted words are the evidence.

newPage.exampleJd:
Customer Success Team Lead

We're looking for a Customer Success Team Lead to run a team of six account managers looking after 300 business customers across the Gulf.

What you'll do
- Lead, coach and plan the work of six account managers
- Own renewals and spot accounts at risk early, using usage data and customer conversations
- Handle escalations with senior customer stakeholders
- Work with product and support to fix the problems customers raise most
- Report on retention and satisfaction to the Head of Customer Experience

What you bring
- 5+ years in customer success or account management, including 2 leading people
- Comfortable with numbers: you can find the story in a renewal forecast
- Calm, clear communication in difficult conversations
- Arabic and English

report.profileNote: Levels with ranges. Wider ranges mean less evidence. Open a domain to see sub-skills and the quotes behind each score.
report.noEvidence: No direct evidence; inferred from related answers.
report.potentialNote: Strengths beyond what this role asks for.
report.developmentNote: Phrased as what to build next, each with evidence.
report.conditional: Some patterns appeared only under certain conditions, such as time pressure. They may not show in calmer settings.
report.styleNote: Tendencies, not scores. Neither end is better.
report.interviewNote: Questions that probe where the assessment is least certain.

none.style: Work style wasn't measured in this session.

method.p1: The candidate worked through one continuous story at a fictional company. The assessment adapted as they answered: it formed hypotheses about their strengths and gaps, tested each in different-looking situations, and raised the difficulty to find their ceiling.
method.p2: Each answer was scored against written descriptions of five levels for each sub-skill. Every score quotes the candidate's own words. Length, grammar, accent and fluency are not scored.
method.ai: Scenarios and scoring used Claude. Important answers were scored twice independently; where the passes disagreed by more than a level, a third pass decided ({n} answers were double-scored).
method.offline: This session used Aalim's curated, human-reviewed scenarios and its built-in scorer. Confidence is deliberately conservative.
method.p3: Levels are estimates with ranges. They become more certain as the same skill shows up consistently across different situations.

practice.body: Short scenarios aimed at your goal, with honest feedback and a twist to try.

share.title: Share a verified profile
share.body: Creates a read-only link to your latest profile for an employer or mentor. It shows your levels with evidence but not your practice or coach conversations, and expires in 14 days.

practice.title: Practice Gym
practice.description: Unlimited scenarios on any skill, pitched a little above your current level. Feedback after each one.
practice.roleplayAsWritten: Write what you would say to {name} first, and how you would handle their likely reaction.
practice.didWellNone: Nothing stood out clearly this time. The points on the right are where to start.
practice.expert: What an expert would also consider
practice.approachNote: One way to handle it, not the only right answer.
practice.scoresNote: Practice scores show how this attempt went. Your profile levels change only when you re-assess.
practice.reflectionHint: What will you do differently next time? Your coach can refer to it later.
practice.offlineNote: This feedback comes from Aalim's built-in coach. With an AI model configured, feedback is more specific to your answer.

progress.title: Progress
progress.description: Real level changes, confirmed by re-assessment every 4–6 weeks. No streaks, no points.
progress.emptyBody: Complete your baseline and some practice; your progress appears here.
progress.oneAssessment: One assessment so far. Re-assess after 4–6 weeks of practice to see real change.
progress.levelsNote: A change counts as real only when the new range doesn't overlap the old one.
progress.practiceNote: How often you practised. Consistency matters more than volume.
progress.compareNote: The faint band under each skill is your range on {date}.

coach.title: Coach
coach.description: Talk about your profile, plan your week, or think through a situation. Honest and direct, never flattering.
coach.empty: Ask anything about your profile or your plan.

suggest.s1: Plan my practice for this week
suggest.s2: Why is my lowest area low?
suggest.s3: What should I focus on first?

coach.error: That didn't go through. Try again.

team.title: Teams
team.description: Build around your people's real strengths: see coverage, gaps and who is ready to grow.
team.devToolTitle: A development tool, not a performance review
team.devTool: Team mode helps you develop people and plan work. It must not be used for dismissals, ratings or pay decisions. Members consent, see their own report first, and you never see their answers unless they choose to share them.
team.emptyBody: Create a team, invite its members, and see the team's strengths once they've taken part.
team.overviewDescription: Coverage, gaps and growth for this team.
team.heatmapNamed: Members × domains, coloured by level. Only members who consented, finished and saw their own report are included.
team.heatmapAnon: With fewer than {min} members assessed ({n} so far), only anonymised team totals are shown.
team.anonNote: Anonymised: the bar shows the range across members, the number the team average.
team.noneAssessedBody: Results appear once members have consented, finished and seen their own report.
team.gapsNote: Where the team falls short of its goals, and where it depends on one person.

gap.no_one_strong: No one is strong here yet (highest {level}).
gap.single_point: Only one person is strong here: a single point of failure.

team.noGaps: No clear gaps against the team's goals.
team.needData: Gaps appear once members have taken part.
team.pipelineNote: Who shows readiness for a lead role, from leadership and management evidence.
team.noPipeline: No one shows clear leadership readiness yet.
team.namedOnly: Shown only when at least five members are included.
team.pairingsNote: Complementary strengths for mentoring and projects.
team.noPairings: No strong mentoring pairs stand out.
team.planNote: Grow tracks for the team's gaps. Members see assigned tracks in their own private Grow space.
team.planPrivacy: You see that a track was assigned, not anyone's practice or feedback.
team.footer: Levels are estimates with ranges. Use them to start conversations, never to end them.
team.memberLockedBody: Individual levels are shown only when the member has finished and seen their own report, and at least {min} members are included.
team.memberSharesRaw: This member chose to share their answers, so evidence quotes are shown.
team.memberNoRaw: This member hasn't shared their answers, so you see levels and themes but no quotes.

create.title: Create a team
create.body: Name the team and choose up to four areas it most needs. You can invite members next.
create.name: Team name
create.purposeHint: One or two sentences. Members see it on their invitation.
create.goalsHint: These get more attention in members' assessments and in the gap analysis.

invite.title: Invite team members
invite.body: Each person gets an email explaining what taking part means. Nothing happens without their consent.
invite.label: Email addresses
invite.consentNote: Members decide whether to take part, and whether to share their answers with you.
invite.sent: {count, plural, one {# invitation sent} other {# invitations sent}}
invite.noEmails: Add at least one valid email address.

teamInvite.title: Team development: {team}
teamInvite.intro: {manager} invited you to a team development assessment. It takes about 40 minutes of realistic work scenarios.
teamInvite.devToolTitle: This is for development, not evaluation
teamInvite.devToolBody: The goal is to understand the team's strengths and grow them. It isn't a performance review and must not be used for decisions about your job.

sees.you: You see your full report first, before anyone else.
sees.small: If fewer than five people in the team take part, your manager sees only anonymised team totals.
sees.levels: Otherwise {manager} sees your skill levels and themes.
sees.raw: No one sees your actual answers unless you tick the box below.
sees.leave: You can withdraw at any time from your settings.

teamInvite.agree: I agree to take part in this team assessment.
teamInvite.shareRaw: Also share my answers (quotes) with {manager}. Optional.
teamInvite.alreadyIn: You've already agreed to take part.
teamInvite.signInFirst: {manager} invited you to a team development assessment. Sign in or create an account first: your results belong to you.
teamInvite.ownData: Your account keeps your report private to you.
teamInvite.invalidBody: It may have been withdrawn. Ask the person who invited you for a new one.
teamInvite.reportPendingBody: This usually takes less than a minute.
teamInvite.youFirst: You're seeing your report first. It counts in your team's view only from now on, and only as levels unless you chose to share your answers.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.description: Send assessment events to your applicant tracking system or any HTTPS endpoint. Every delivery is signed so you can verify it came from Aalim.
integrations.addDescription: We POST a JSON payload to this address when the events you choose happen.
integrations.secretBody: This is the only time it is shown. Store it with your ATS integration; use it to verify the X-Aalim-Signature header.
integrations.urlHint: Must be a public HTTPS address.

eventHelp.candidate_started: A candidate gave consent and started the assessment.
eventHelp.candidate_completed: A candidate finished. The report is still being prepared.
eventHelp.report_ready: The report is ready, with role fit and a link to it.

integrations.testSent: Test event sent. Check the delivery log below.
integrations.emptyBody: Add an endpoint above to push results into your ATS.
integrations.confirmDelete: Delete this webhook? Deliveries stop immediately.
integrations.verifyBody: Compute an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body with your secret and compare it with the X-Aalim-Signature header.

errors.invalid: Choose at least one event and enter a URL.
errors.invalidUrl: That doesn't look like a valid URL.
errors.privateHost: Private and internal addresses can't receive webhooks.

fairness.title: Fairness
fairness.description: Score outcomes by voluntary, self-reported group. Only aggregates are shown, and groups smaller than five are hidden.
fairness.flaggedBody: These groups reach the selected fit level at less than 80% of the rate of the highest group (the four-fifths rule). This is a signal to review, not proof of bias: check the role's requirements and the items involved.
fairness.emptyBody: Candidates can answer optional equal-opportunity questions after they finish. Results appear here once there are enough to show safely.
fairness.allSuppressed: Every group has fewer than {n} people, so nothing is shown yet.
fairness.suppressed: {n, plural, one {# person} other {# people}} in groups smaller than {min} not shown.
fairness.validityBody: Compares role-fit scores with the 6- and 12-month performance ratings managers record on reports.
fairness.validityTooFew: {n, plural, =0 {No ratings recorded yet.} one {# rating recorded.} other {# ratings recorded.}} We show a correlation from 20 ratings, so that it means something.
fairness.validityResult: Correlation between role fit and later performance: r = {r} (from {n} ratings).
fairness.method: Method: answers are voluntary and stored apart from assessments. Selection rate is the share of a group at or above the chosen fit level; impact ratio divides it by the highest group's rate. Ratios below 80% are flagged. Choose the level that matches how your team actually uses results.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.description: Who did what in your organisation: report views, shares, exports, invitations, settings and data deletion.
audit.emptyBody: Activity appears here as your team works.
audit.retentionNote: Audit records are kept for as long as the organisation exists. Deleting a candidate removes their data, but the fact that it was deleted stays here.

library.title: Competency library
library.description: Add the skills your organisation cares about beyond the built-in framework, with your own behavioural anchors.
library.explainer: Library skills sit inside a framework domain and can be added to any assessment in its setup. Claude writes scenarios for them and scores against your anchors. The curated offline bank only covers the built-in framework, so library skills need AI generation turned on to be measured.
library.invalid: Fill in the name, description and all five anchors in English.
library.formHint: Anchors describe what someone does at each level, in observable terms. Editing a skill creates a new version; existing reports keep the version they used.
library.arabicHint: Optional. Anything left empty falls back to English.
library.name: Name

anchorPlaceholder.1: What does someone at this level actually do or miss?
anchorPlaceholder.2: Gets the basics right with support…
anchorPlaceholder.3: Does it reliably on their own…
anchorPlaceholder.4: Handles hard cases and helps others…

library.emptyBody: Start with one skill that's specific to how your organisation works.

itemReview.title: Item bank review
itemReview.description: How each curated item performs in live use. Flags appear once an item has been answered {n} times.
itemReview.retireBody: Retired items are never selected again. Sessions that already used it keep their scores.
itemReview.notePlaceholder: What's wrong with it, for the next reviewer

dataRights.title: Your data
dataRights.description: Take a copy of everything Aalim holds about you, or delete it.
dataRights.exportBody: Your profile, assessments, answers, reports, practice and coach conversations, as a JSON file.
dataRights.deleteBody: Removes your account and every assessment, answer, report and development record. This can't be undone.
dataRights.confirmTitle: Delete your account and all your data?
dataRights.confirmBody: Organisations you were assessed by will see that a deletion happened, but not what was deleted. You'll be signed out.

errors.confirmMismatch: That doesn't match your email address.
errors.lastAdmin: You're the only admin of an organisation with other members. Make someone else an admin first.

outcomes.title: After the hire
outcomes.description: If you hired this person, rate their performance later. Aalim compares these ratings with assessment results to check it predicts what matters.
outcomes.privacy: Ratings are used only in aggregate, to validate the assessment. They never change the report.
outcomes.deleteBody: Permanently removes the assessment, answers, scores and report.
outcomes.confirmBody: The assessment, every answer, score and report will be removed. The audit log keeps a record that it was deleted. This can't be undone.
outcomes.confirmLabel: Type the candidate's name to confirm

brandbook.title: Aalim brand
brandbook.metaDescription: How Aalim looks, sounds and behaves: the brand platform, logo, colour, type, voice and assets.

hero.intro: How Aalim looks, sounds and behaves, in English and Arabic. Everything here is built from the same components and tokens as the product, so it can’t drift.

story.title: One word, two meanings
story.body1: In Arabic, the same four letters spell ʿālim, someone who knows a subject deeply, and ʿālam, a world.
story.body2: Aalim builds a world for each person, a realistic week at a fictional company, and finds out what they know in it. The name is the product.
story.usage: Write Aalim in English text and عالم in Arabic. The lowercase “aalim” appears only in the wordmark.

platform.title: What we stand for
platform.positioning: For organisations that hire and develop people, Aalim is the skills assessment that shows its working: realistic scenarios that adapt to every answer, and every score backed by the person’s own words.

evidence.title: Show the evidence
evidence.body: Every claim links to the person’s own words. If we can’t quote it, we don’t say it.

certainty.title: Be honest about certainty
certainty.body: Ranges, not verdicts. We say how sure we are, in plain words.

people.title: People decide
people.body: Aalim informs decisions about people. It never makes them, and it never rejects anyone.

fair.title: Fair by design
fair.body: Checked for adverse impact, accessible to everyone, private by default.

bilingual.title: Bilingual from the first line
bilingual.body: Arabic and English are equals. Neither is a translation added later.

voice.title: How we sound

specific.title: Specific over impressive
specific.body: “Spotted that station 2 closes at noon” beats “strong analytical skills”.

ranges.title: Numbers with ranges and reasons
ranges.body: Give the level, the range and why. Never a bare percentage.

calm.title: Calm
calm.body: No exclamation marks, no urgency tricks, no hype words like “revolutionary” or “AI-powered”.

verbs.title: Verbs on buttons
verbs.body: Sentence case and active voice. A button says what happens: “Publish”, then “Published”.

candidates.title: To candidates
candidates.body: Calm and reassuring, clear about what happens to their data.
candidates.example: Take the time you need. Your answers save as you type.

teams.title: To hiring teams
teams.body: Precise and brief. Lead with what to do next.

growth.title: To people growing
growth.example: You named the trade-off. An expert would also check who else the delay affects.

examples: You were strongest at evaluating evidence.
Scenarios adapt as people answer. Every score quotes their own words.
Partial fit. Below the expected level on management: explore it in the interview.

logo.title: Logo
logo.symbolBody: The narrowing range in miniature: a scale, the band where the person’s level probably lies, and the estimate inside it. The band is saffron because saffron always means evidence.
logo.wordmarkBody: “aalim” in Alexandria Semibold, with the dot of the i in saffron: the evidence, again. عالم is set in the same typeface, on the same baseline, separated by a hairline.
logo.clearSpace: Clear space: at least the height of the band on every side.
logo.minSize: Minimum size: symbol 16 px; bilingual lockup 120 px wide.

donts.recolour: Recolour the dot or the band
donts.busy: Place it on saffron or busy images
donts.redraw: Retype the wordmark in another font

colour.title: Colour
colour.body: Mostly quiet stone, one deep ink for brand moments, indigo only for actions, saffron only for evidence.

ink.name: Ink
ink.role: Brand surfaces: verdicts, chapter cards, hero panels.

indigo.name: Indigo
indigo.role: Primary actions, focus and current selection. Nothing else.

saffron.name: Saffron
saffron.role: Evidence and the dot in the logo. Never decoration.

stone.name: Stone
stone.role: Backgrounds, text and borders: most of every screen.

levels.name: Level ramp
levels.role: Skill levels and role fit. One hue, never red and green.

colour.darkNote: Every colour has a dark-mode pair, and every text pairing is tested for WCAG AA contrast.

type.title: Type
type.displayBody: Drawn for Latin and Arabic together, so both languages share one voice. Page titles, verdicts, big numbers.
type.textTitle: IBM Plex Sans and Plex Sans Arabic, for text
type.textBody: One family designed to pair across scripts. Precise without being cold. Everything else.
type.sampleText: Every score in Aalim comes with a range, a confidence and the person’s own words.
type.rules: Arabic gets more line height (1.65 for text, 1.32 for display) and no letter spacing. Numbers use Latin digits by default; Arabic-Indic digits are a personal setting.

signatures.title: Signatures
signatures.rangeBody: Every estimate is drawn as a band on the 1–5 scale. It narrows as evidence comes in, and a tick marks the level the role expects. It is the brand’s one moving idea.
signatures.evidenceBody: The candidate’s verbatim words are marked in saffron, the way a careful reviewer marks a quote.
signatures.evidenceSample: Before I answer the client, I’d check
signatures.evidenceMark: whether the delay affects the other two orders on the same route.
signatures.fieldBody: Rows of estimates narrowing from lavender (uncertain) to saffron (evidenced). A texture for brand surfaces and social images, never inside the product.

imagery.title: Imagery, icons and motion
imagery.imageryBody: Show the product and the range field. If you show people, show real workplaces in the region, in natural light, doing work rather than posing. Never robots, brains or circuit boards for “AI”.
imagery.iconsBody: Lucide, 1.75 stroke, 16 or 20 px, in text or secondary colour. Never multicolour.
imagery.motionBody: One orchestrated moment per page at most: the band narrowing. Everything else responds to the person in 150–250 ms, and all of it stops under reduced motion.

downloads.title: Downloads
downloads.body: Outlined vector files (no font needed) and PNG renders, generated from the brand fonts by npm run brand:assets.
